calls.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset: one finished STATIC PIXEL-ART VISUAL STUDY for the game "那天之后", not a poster, no UI, no writing or panel border.
The two input images are world/anatomy reference images, NOT edit targets. Retain their profound alien scale and dry horn/fibre living matter. Redesign their visual organization for a legible pixel game; do not reproduce their dense realistic microtexture.

SAME SCENE to preserve across our three camera studies:
A lone ordinary human traveller with an ochre-brown coat, small backpack, modest warm shoulder lamp and short crowbar stands on the broad surface of an immense living body. The body is an asymmetrical crescent-shaped, thick mantle, with a gently cupped upper surface, a tapered curling outer lip and a fibrous underside. Its upper surface offers a broad unbroken place to stand and walk, part of the anatomy, without a constructed path. This body is NOT an island of earth: the curling edge exposes the continuous layers of the body.
There are exactly two especially readable connections in the local scene: at its inner left shoulder, a thick fan of living fibres merges into a much larger upright mantle above/behind; at its outer right lip, a second separate curved body rises from far below, its blunt folded end pressing against and supporting the underside. Show that contact fully, as broad compressive folds bearing weight, not a rope tied to a point. The supporter then continues down into the air and connects with a further large low-contrast mantle in the distance. We must follow support across at least two bodies. Empty air between these connections is crucial. Do not fill the air with root spaghetti.
On the upper surface near the inner shoulder are three broad offset growth folds; these, the left fan and the right under-support are the visual landmarks common to all views. An irregular small opening near the far rim can show air through the body. Surrounding life extends beyond the frame at other depths, but the clear local connection is the subject.

AESTHETIC:
Deliberate hand-authored-looking pixel art with decisive stepped contours, grouped planar pixel clusters and restrained local shading. Broad restful shapes, not stippled texture everywhere. Physically deep forms drawn in pixels, not a smooth low-poly 3D render or a painted image with a noisy pixel filter. Near layers can be richly but selectively drawn; far silhouettes much simpler. Organic dry layered horn, aged fibrous umber, dusty ochre ridges, desaturated violet-brown shadow planes; cool mineral-grey air separates the warm living bodies. Use the references as a family, with more legible value separation and less surface noise. The world feels ancient, alien, immense and quietly unsettling. No ordinary trees, leaves, mushroom caps, rocky floating islands, gore, eyes, teeth, buildings, railings, grids, neon, decorative magic or fantasy hero. Alien life is conveyed through continuous mantle anatomy, growth folds and pressure at contact, not recognizable animal parts. Strong quiet masses of air are allowed to be lighter than the bodies. No blanket black fog hiding the scene.

Keep the traveller visible and readable at ordinary screen size, roughly 4 percent of image height, feet firmly resting on the upper surface. Show a small clear contact shadow, no spotlight disk. The immediate anatomy and empty air must be understandable without labels or arrows. One landscape image, 3:2 composition.

CAMERA STUDY A — SIDEWARD DEPTH:
Observe from the side, only about 10–15 degrees above the traveller's standing surface. Compose the traveller at the left third, seen in three-quarter profile. The main mantle traverses the middle-lower portion from a huge inner shoulder at the left to a curled tip on the right. We see a narrow but unmistakably broad-in-depth upper walking surface and a deep continuous belly beneath it. The supporting lower body must be fully readable against lighter open air on the right, rising and cupping the outer underside; its connection onward to a lower distant mantle is visible through the largest gap.
The upper/inner fan rises diagonally behind the traveller, not in front of them. Bodies stagger through substantial lateral depth, with a far wall of immense low-contrast mantle silhouettes and atmospheric gaps. This is a sideward view THROUGH the colony, not top-down isometric, and not a vertical slice with black cutaway sides. Strong distinct silhouettes, enough sparse background to understand how this inhabited body fits into the colony. All ground ends belong to curling living anatomy. Finish the pixel artwork with the discipline of a polished game's actual camera frame, not a title-screen illustration.

Use case: style-transfer.
Edit target: the attached generated sideward visual study.
Preserve its camera, scene, body silhouettes, traveller, three growth folds on the upper surface, right-hand supporting contact and open air exactly. Redraw ONLY the image's pixel-art mark making and detail hierarchy.

The current image has too many small sandy flecks and evenly detailed ridges. Make it read like deliberate finished 2D pixel artwork rather than a detailed digital painting. Group the upper body's walking surface into broad mostly quiet ochre/mauve pixel shapes. Keep only a few carefully chosen large growth folds. Shade each turn with 3–5 controlled flat color clusters, with hard stepped contours and sparse selected breakup. On the fibrous belly, retain the strongest load-bearing ribs; most fine parallel hatching and sparkly edge specks should disappear. Detail concentrates at the right supporting contact and near the small traveller. Render remote colonies as quiet silhouettes and large stepped color areas with no granular texture. Air is made of calm broad muted value bands, without photographic mist or tiny dither.

The result should have visibly intentional pixel clusters at normal screen size: spacious, graphic, materially dry and bodily, still immense. Keep subtle dusty warm horn versus cool grey-violet air, readable depth and all existing anatomical support relationships. Do not add lines, labels, borders, objects, characters, stone blocks or a global mosaic filter. One landscape 3:2 image.
calls.outcome: superseded: hole and hooked rim suggest a bird head

calls.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Create ONE PIXEL-ART STATIC CAMERA STUDY, landscape 3:2, without any title, text, arrows or UI.
Input image: the original world concept, used only for alien horn/fibre anatomy and immense airborne depth. It is not an edit target. Replace its realistic painting with deliberate pixel clusters and a fresh local composition.

CRITICAL CAMERA/COMPOSITION:
A visibly PERSPECTIVE scene viewed from behind a small human traveller, looking LENGTHWISE along a broad living mantle extending AWAY from the camera INTO THE PAGE. The main walkface starts as a wide rounded crescent in the bottom foreground and narrows through foreshortening towards a towering bodily shoulder around the upper middle of the image. The near and far ridges have strongly different apparent sizes. This is a continuous 3D-space composition illustrated in pixels. Do not draw a side profile of a horizontal bridge spanning from the left edge to the right edge. Do not use a high isometric camera. No separate foreground pasted over a flat background. One coherent approximately 20-degree downward perspective view, with a deep view through the right side of the frame.

The SAME local anatomy for our three-view study:
The human stands on a huge dry living mantle, not soil or a built platform. Three broad separated anatomical growth folds on the upper face recede toward a huge inner fan, which fans into a larger upright body in the upper-middle distance. The surface is gently cupped, broad enough for free movement. The body's near outer lip at bottom-right folds downward in two thick blunt layered hems, with no sharp hooked tip and no eye-like holes.
A DIFFERENT thick curved body rises from deep below on the right and presses its blunt folded end against that near outer lip from underneath. Show the weight-bearing junction clearly at the near-right corner, beside and below the traveller, with compressed layers where they meet. It must belong to another body, continuing down the open right-hand gap into an atmospheric depth layer where a further mantle supports it. The upper body/fan recedes away into depth, whereas this other supporter rises from below towards the near foreground. Keep enough of this support and its downward continuation visible.
All life bodies interconnect but hold large, spacious pockets of empty air between them. No ultimate ground. Farther to the right, smaller distant mantles recede among quiet grey-violet atmospheric layers. The top of frame is partly occupied by the vast overhanging body receiving the inner fan, but important walking/contact forms remain visible.

CHARACTER AND STYLE:
Exactly one small, ordinary traveller near the bottom centre, seen from behind, ochre-brown coat, little pack, short crowbar held at the side, one muted warm shoulder lamp. Around 5 percent image height, readable silhouette and grounded feet, no heroic pose. Muted dusty ochre horn, umber/violet-brown shadow planes and cool grey-violet air. Keep the upper surface calmer/lighter than the turning edge and underside.
Draw restrained, visibly handmade-looking PIXEL ART, hard stepped silhouettes and large organized color clusters, roughly 3–5 flat local tones per surface. Large restful planes with a few strong growth folds, selective details at joints and character, simple distant silhouettes. Not photorealistic, not smooth voxel or low-poly CGI, no global mosaic filter, no dense stippled gravel or tiny texture everywhere. Alien dry layered mantle tissue, not tree bark, rock ledges, a giant animal face, a mushroom, gore or architecture. Quiet vastness with readable air, not a blanket of black. Preserve material kinship with the concept but simplify aggressively.
The single purpose of this frame is to make the viewer feel they are standing on a continuous immense body that leads INTO the colony, while the adjacent downward support remains understandable.
